quotes.text: What do you think about the dangers and risks of the government potentially funding and moving toward algorithms that use AI technology to censor Americans online?

Snapchat admitted that their AI technology [...] is experimental, so do you agree that it is alarming and problematic that Snapchat would force their users, which comprise almost 60 percent of American teens, to use their chatbot features unless they paid to disable it with a subscription service? [...] If you do not want it, you have to pay to get it off, if you want to keep using Snapchat.

Artificial intelligence surely has productive uses, but it can also present great threats, especially to our children. [...] Today I am introducing my AI Shield for Kids (ASK) Act, to prevent children from accessing artificial intelligence features on social media sites without the consent of a parent or guardian.

The CFPB has been leading a number of efforts on artificial intelligence, and we're working to bring on more technical talent inside the agency. We're taking steps to guard against algorithmic bias across credit markets, and we're working to ensure that data brokers respect longstanding laws on the books.

Despite it being labeled a rule on artificial intelligence, your power grab to regulate emerging and existing technologies—even Excel spreadsheets—is beyond the SEC's scope and will ultimately stifle innovation.

I am deeply concerned about another proposed midnight rule being floated by the lame-duck Biden administration. This time, it is related to export controls on advanced computing and artificial intelligence.

But it also poses risks. Algorithms can replicate and even accelerate bias. Data points such as graduation dates or years of experience can serve as proxies for age, leading to older applicants being screened out automatically. Policymakers must ensure AI is used to expand opportunity, not entrench age discrimination, by supporting upskilling programs and enforcing protections against algorithmic bias.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping our markets and our economy, and the United States must stay ahead of China.

As Chairman of @BankingGOP, I’m focused on policies that boost innovation, protect our sensitive technologies, and keep America competitive.

I think it's really important for us to realize that we still have the high ground and maintaining the high ground means having an aggressive posture against China. [...] That means everything from how we review our sanctions, to how we take a look at [the] chip conversation that you've seen over the last several days, [and] artificial intelligence being a part of that conversation as well.
Yes, AI and the data centers will use more power but provide their own power, pay for it. So, what could happen ultimately is a subsidy for our electricity ratepayers, not a burden on our ratepayers.

AI should empower American workers, not replace them.

Combined with the talent, grit, and ingenuity of the American workforce, AI can boost productivity, raise incomes, and create more opportunity. https://t.co/qJGUvZtkh5
AI is a powerful tool. Like any powerful tool, it brings both opportunity and risk. We should not run from this potential, but we should also not ignore the risks.
We need thoughtful and well-informed solutions that protect Americans and mitigate major risks without hampering innovation or pushing it overseas.

The United States cannot afford to let China or any other adversary gain a technological edge in artificial intelligence. [...] The world’s tech stack, including powerful AI tools, must be built on trusted U.S. networks and technology.

AI should be a tool that strengthens American workers, not one that makes them feel replaceable. [...] There is dignity in work, and if America leads, AI can help workers build skills, support their families, and create new opportunities in South Carolina and all across this great nation.
We know artificial intelligence is coming. The number one objective we have is to protect our consumers and make sure they don’t bear the burden of higher costs in electricity or water usage.

The one thing we all agree upon, left and right, is that China will not lead in AI. The stack will be built by American companies, American products, and America’s vision for the future of the world, not China’s.

Artificial intelligence is going to increase productivity, which will increase wages without seeing a significant drop in employment. [...] Augmentation is really important, not automation. Augmentation means that people will do more work with more opportunities and more resources because of artificial intelligence. They won’t lose their jobs.

The question is simple: who wins the future, China or America?
 
Artificial intelligence will help decide the answer. I am fighting to make sure America leads. https://t.co/8oceXMXKqP

While artificial intelligence, powered by these data centers, is important to the future of America, we must make sure it is integrated into our lives responsibly. Innovative technologies should not be rushed carelessly at the expense of S.C. families.

South Carolinians are rightfully concerned about how AI will affect our lives. But I’m confident that as a nation, we will discover ways to responsibly address AI’s potential dangers while tapping into its possibilities to better our lives.

America has led the world through innovation, and AI should be no different. By holding companies to their commitments, we can make sure South Carolinians power the future of innovation without forcing our greatest resources - our people - to bear the cost. https://t.co/LbtAihRinK

Foreign adversaries shouldn't get to steal what American innovators built.

Proud to join @SenatorHagerty and @SenatorAndyKim on the BLADE Act to expose and punish the bad actors behind these attacks on American artificial intelligence.

But we also know that Democrats are being used as pawns for this disinformation campaign run by China to make sure that China wins the AI future instead of America. We absolutely have to make sure that data centers only go to communities that want them and they pay their own way.
